title: dedicated: unified-priority-routing + burst controls + utilization reporting
author: Maya Chen
ci_details: build: pass; unit: pass; integration: pass (flaky test xretry fixed); lint: pass; e2e: pass on canary cluster
description:
Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets reported two issues under load: 1) high-priority traffic occasionally starves lower-priority customers during bursts, causing noisy neighbor behavior; 2) lack of per-fleet utilization metrics made it hard for SREs and sales to reason about committed throughput vs actual usage. This PR implements (a) a unified priority-routing policy in the Dedicated autoscaler that respects throughput guarantees while enabling bounded bursts, (b) token-bucket smoothing and backpressure hooks to avoid transient queue growth, and (c) additional utilization reporting metrics exported to observability (per-fleet throughput, burst_consumed_tokens, smoothed_utilization_pct) and a small Console dashboard wiring.

Changes included: consolidated routing rules (priority -> capacity-class -> regional-fallback), new BurstController with configurable max_burst_tokens and smoothing_half_life, token-bucket based admission with early-failure path, updated autoscaler reconciliation to account for reserved throughput guarantees when scaling up, and 2 new Prometheus metrics + tracing spans for burst decisions. Also includes unit and integration tests, docs and a Linear link for rollout plan. See checklist below.
commits: initial: add priority routing scaffold and policy objects
autoscaler: implement tokenbucket admission and smoothing (BurstController)
reports: export per-fleet metrics (throughput_rps, burst_consumed_tokens, smoothed_utilization_pct)
runtime: integrate admission hooks into request router and KV cache path
tests: add unit/integration tests for burst smoothing and priority routing
docs: update dedicated autoscaler config docs + Console wiring
fix: address flaky TestBurstSmoothing by increasing retry window and test isolation
chore: update changelog and release notes
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Overall approach looks good. Two asks: 1) add a knob for smoothing half-life per-fleet (so enterprise customers can tune), 2) add an integration test that simulates region fallback under burst load.

Maya Chen: addressed both requests in commits 3 and 5. smoothing_half_life is now configurable in autoscaler_types.go and surfaced to defaults.yaml. Added integration test burst_smoking_test.go that exercises region fallback.
Priya Shah: CI flakes on TestBurstSmoothing were caused by shared global clock in tests; recommend using fake clock. Thanks for the fix in tests.
Liam O'Connor: +1 after docs update and Prometheus metric name change (smoothed_utilization_pct -> fleet_smoothed_utilization_percent). Confirmed dashboards render in canary.
merge_outcome: squash and merge by Maya Chen after approvals. Rollout plan: canary to customers with dedicated fleets for 48h, monitor 'fleet_smoothed_utilization_percent' and 'burst_reject_rate' and rollback on >1% sustained rejection for paying fleets.
tests: unit: pass (100% for modified packages); integration: pass on canary cluster; stress: ran 30m soak with synthetic traffic; flaky tests retried and stabilized
release_notes: Added priority-aware autoscaler routing with bounded burst controls and per-fleet utilization metrics. Config knobs: max_burst_tokens, smoothing_half_life, guarantee_reservation_pct. Improves isolation between priority classes and provides new observability metrics for Dedicated fleet owners.
notes_for_ops: During rollout, enable debug logging for autoscaler: REDWOOD_AUTOSCALER_DEBUG=true for canary clusters. Watch metrics: fleet_smoothed_utilization_percent, burst_consumed_tokens, burst_reject_rate, autoscaler_scale_events. Default smoothing_half_life=15s; enterprise customers may increase to 60s if they run highly spiky workloads.
backport: release/2026-02 (manual backport required due to config schema change)
